Subject: Temporary backup custody request — evidence retention carveout

Hi Hannah,

We're kicking off a regulatory readiness audit and Legal has asked us to confirm that Redwood can pause deletion of backups and certain operational logs for a 90-day window so we can produce forensic evidence if required. Specifically: 

- Hold backups containing Medicore tenant data for 90 days (no purge).
- Retain operational logs (auth logs, request traces, and access audits) for the same 90-day window.
- Provide a short DPA addendum that authorizes the temporary retention and confirms subprocessors and transfer boundaries.

Two quick questions: will this require any cross-border transfer (we're primarily EU-origin data for a subset of users), and which subprocessors (if any) would be involved in the backups?

I've attached the audit_request_form.pdf with the request details and the compliance deadline. Can you let us know whether Redwood can accept this carveout and what next steps / documents you need?

Thanks,
Liam Torres
Senior Compliance Manager
Medicore Health

Proposed immediate plan:
- Redwood to pause purge of backups and flagged logs for 90 days starting 2026-09-27 (window can be adjusted if you need a different start date).
- We'll provide a redlined DPA addendum for Medicore to sign that explicitly authorizes the hold and identifies the retained categories (backups + auth/request/access logs).
- Compliance will confirm whether any subprocessors are engaged for backup storage/replication and whether EU transfers are implicated.

I've looped in Kimberly (Trust & Legal) and Karthik (Solutions) to validate operating constraints and prepare the addendum. Expect a compliance reply within 24–48 hours and a DPA draft shortly after.

Hannah / team,

Thanks — we can support Medicore's request under a controlled addendum. Summary of compliance assessment and required controls: 

1) Scope & duration: approve a timeboxed 90-day hold (2026-09-27 to 2026-12-26) limited to the specified tenant IDs. Any extension must be requested in writing and undergo a formal review.

2) DPA addendum: we will issue a short-form addendum that:
   - explicitly authorizes the temporary retention and lists the retained categories,
   - requires Medicore to provide the tenant IDs and the designated evidence custodian,
   - limits use of retained data to audit/forensic production only,
   - sets deletion timeline and verification steps at the end of the window.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: preliminary check indicates backups are stored in a Redwood-managed S3 replica (vendor: CloudBlob Storage partner). That subprocessor will be notified and must acknowledge the addendum. For EU-origin data: we will keep data in EU region where possible; if any replication crosses borders we'll log transfers and include them in the addendum.

4) Operational constraints: we will mark the matching snapshots/log buckets with a retention hold flag that suspends normal purge jobs. This is a manual safety net — ops runbooks will include an override lock and audit log.

5) Evidence & verification: we will provide a proof bundle (hash list + snapshot locator) and SOC2 Type II summary. We need DocuSign-signed addendum before we enact the hold.

6) Tracking & escalation: create Jira INFR-3421 to track scope, subprocessor notifications, and the purge-unhold task. If anything urgent appears (data access or legal order), escalate immediately to Trust: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com.

I've attached a redline of the proposed addendum (Redline_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf) and a short SOC2 summary (SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf) for Medicore to review. Once Medicore signs, Ops will enact the flag within 4 business hours.

Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Legal
Redwood Inference
